```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)

# This is the same prepared data file used by the Question 10 dashboard.
vehicles <- read_csv("../dashboard_q10/fuel_economy.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Recalculate the numbers whenever the presentation is knitted.
n_configurations <- nrow(vehicles)
mean_mpg <- mean(vehicles$combined_mpg)
mean_gap <- mean(vehicles$highway_mpg - vehicles$city_mpg)
class_summary <- vehicles %>%
  group_by(vehicle_group) %>%
  summarise(median_mpg = median(combined_mpg), .groups = "drop")
cars_median <- class_summary$median_mpg[class_summary$vehicle_group == "Cars"]
pickups_median <- class_summary$median_mpg[class_summary$vehicle_group == "Pickups"]
```

<main id="stage" aria-label="Car Fuel Economy presentation">

<!-- Slide 1: Car Fuel Economy -->
<section class="slide cover" aria-label="Car Fuel Economy" data-slide="1">
<h2>Car Fuel Economy</h2>
<div class="subtitle">MATH 421 Final Project</div>
<div class="read-aloud">
<p>An interactive dashboard for EPA vehicle configurations, 2015–2025.</p>
</div>
<div class="page">1 / 10</div>
</section>

<!-- Slide 2: The data -->
<section class="slide" aria-label="The data" data-slide="2">
<h2>The data</h2>
<div class="read-aloud">
<p>The source is FuelEconomy.gov. The prepared file has 12,381 gasoline and diesel configurations.</p>
<p>A row is a vehicle configuration, such as a model with a particular engine and transmission. It is not a vehicle sale.</p>
<p>Non-plug-in hybrids are included. Electric, plug-in, flexible-fuel, and dual-fuel vehicles are excluded.</p>
</div>
<div class="source-note">Source: <a href="https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/download.shtml">FuelEconomy.gov</a> | Data downloaded November 18, 2026</div>
<div class="page">2 / 10</div>
</section>

<!-- Slide 3: Five different inputs -->
<section class="slide" aria-label="Five different inputs" data-slide="3">
<h2>Five different inputs</h2>
<div class="read-aloud">
<p>The dropdown selects a manufacturer. Checkboxes select vehicle groups.</p>
<p>The slider selects model years. Radio buttons select gasoline, diesel, or both.</p>
<p>The numeric input sets the maximum engine size. All five inputs filter the same dataset.</p>
</div>
<div class="page">3 / 10</div>
</section>

<!-- Slide 4: Dashboard features -->
<section class="slide" aria-label="Dashboard features" data-slide="4">
<h2>Dashboard features</h2>
<div class="read-aloud">
<p>Overview shows three value boxes, a findings paragraph, and the yearly MPG plot.</p>
<p>Group Comparisons uses tabs for vehicle groups and manufacturer rankings. Engine and Driving has two scatterplots.</p>
<p>Vehicle Data has a searchable table. About the Data explains the source, cleaning, and limitations.</p>
</div>
<div class="page">4 / 10</div>
</section>

<!-- Slide 5: Results with all filters open -->
<section class="slide results" aria-label="Results with all filters open" data-slide="5">
<h2>Results with all filters open</h2>

```{r median-mpg-chart, results='asis'}
# Compare the group medians using the same data as the dashboard.
median_plot <- ggplot(class_summary,
                      aes(x = reorder(vehicle_group, -median_mpg), y = median_mpg)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(aes(label = median_mpg), vjust = -.3, size = 6) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 30)) +
  labs(x = "Vehicle group", y = "Median MPG") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18)

# Embed the R plot in the HTML so there is no separate image to upload.
plot_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
ggsave(plot_file, plot = median_plot, width = 11, height = 3, dpi = 150)
cat('<img class="plot" alt="Median combined MPG by vehicle group" src="',
    knitr::image_uri(plot_file), '">', sep = "")
```

<div class="read-aloud">
<p>The `r format(n_configurations, big.mark = ",")` configurations average `r sprintf("%.1f", mean_mpg)` combined MPG.</p>
<p>Highway MPG is `r sprintf("%.1f", mean_gap)` higher than city MPG on average. Cars have a median combined MPG of `r cars_median`, compared with `r pickups_median` for pickups.</p>
<p>These comparisons give every configuration equal weight. They do not represent the mix of vehicles people bought.</p>
</div>
<div class="page">5 / 10</div>
</section>

<!-- Slide 6: How the code is organized -->
<section class="slide" aria-label="How the code is organized" data-slide="6">
<h2>How the code is organized</h2>
<div class="read-aloud">
<p>Setup loads the packages and reads the prepared CSV once.</p>
<p>The sidebar creates the five inputs. Output chunks create places for plots, values, and the table.</p>
<p>The server chunk uses reactive() to filter the rows. renderPlotly(), renderText(), renderUI(), and renderDT() fill the outputs.</p>
</div>
<div class="page">6 / 10</div>
</section>

<!-- Slide 7: How the filtering works -->
<section class="slide code-slide" aria-label="How the filtering works" data-slide="7">
<h2>How the filtering works</h2>
<pre><code>filtered &lt;- reactive({
  d &lt;- df %&gt;%
    filter(vehicle_group %in% input$groups,
           year &gt;= input$years[1],
           year &lt;= input$years[2],
           engine_l &lt;= input$engine_max)
  # Manufacturer and fuel filters follow.
})</code></pre>
<div class="read-aloud">
<p>reactive() recalculates when an input changes. Each output calls filtered() so the figures use the same selection.</p>
</div>
<div class="page">7 / 10</div>
</section>

<!-- Slide 8: Challenges and fixes -->
<section class="slide" aria-label="Challenges and fixes" data-slide="8">
<h2>Challenges and fixes</h2>
<div class="read-aloud">
<p>MPG and electric MPGe have different meanings. The project focuses on single-fuel gasoline and diesel configurations.</p>
<p>Empty filters can leave no rows. Each plot checks the row count and shows a message instead of an unexplained blank plot.</p>
<p>The live image folder needs a Shiny resource path. The value boxes use value_box() so their numbers can update.</p>
</div>
<div class="page">8 / 10</div>
</section>

<!-- Slide 9: A simple live demonstration -->
<section class="slide" aria-label="A simple live demonstration" data-slide="9">
<h2>A simple live demonstration</h2>
<div class="read-aloud">
<p>Start with all filters open and read the summary values.</p>
<p>Choose Toyota, keep only SUVs, choose Gasoline, and set the maximum engine size to 2.5 liters.</p>
<p>Open the comparison tabs and the Vehicle Data page. Search for RAV4. The sidebar filters the full dashboard; table search filters only the table.</p>
</div>
<div class="page">9 / 10</div>
</section>

<!-- Slide 10: Advice for this project -->
<section class="slide" aria-label="Advice for this project" data-slide="10">
<h2>Advice for this project</h2>
<div class="read-aloud">
<p>Build a small dashboard first, then add one input and one output at a time.</p>
<p>Keep the prepared CSV and image folder with the QMD. Use relative paths so the app can run on the server.</p>
<p>Test empty selections and check the numbers. Publish the Shiny app on Posit Connect Cloud because HTML alone cannot run its inputs.</p>
</div>
<div class="page">10 / 10</div>
</section>
</main>
<nav id="controls" aria-label="Presentation controls"><button id="prev" aria-label="Previous slide">Previous</button><button id="next" aria-label="Next slide">Next</button><button id="full">Full screen</button></nav>
<script>


(()=>{
 const slides=Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.slide'));
 let current=Math.max(0,Math.min(slides.length-1,parseInt(location.hash.slice(1),10)-1||0));
 function show(n){current=Math.max(0,Math.min(slides.length-1,n));slides.forEach((s,i)=>{s.classList.toggle('active',i===current);s.setAttribute('aria-hidden',i!==current)});history.replaceState(null,'','#'+(current+1));document.title='Car Fuel Economy: '+(current+1)+' / '+slides.length;}
 function fit(){document.getElementById('stage').style.transform='translate(-50%,-50%) scale('+Math.min(innerWidth/1280,innerHeight/720)+')'}
 document.getElementById('prev').onclick=()=>show(current-1);
 document.getElementById('next').onclick=()=>show(current+1);
 document.getElementById('full').onclick=()=>{if(document.fullscreenElement)document.exitFullscreen();else document.documentElement.requestFullscreen?.()};
 addEventListener('keydown',e=>{if(['ArrowRight','PageDown',' '].includes(e.key)){e.preventDefault();show(current+1)}else if(['ArrowLeft','PageUp'].includes(e.key)){e.preventDefault();show(current-1)}else if(e.key==='Home')show(0);else if(e.key==='End')show(slides.length-1);else if(e.key.toLowerCase()==='f')document.getElementById('full').click()});
 addEventListener('resize',fit);show(current);fit();
})();

</script>
